sectionsUsed: PostgreSQL Downloads: ready-to-use packages or installers for Linux, macOS, Windows, BSD and Solaris, or a source archive (cheat sheet install note)
1.1 Installation: PostgreSQL must be installed before use, may already be installed, and can be installed by an unprivileged user
1.3 Creating a Database: a running PostgreSQL server can manage many databases, typically one per project or user (o1 teaching)
1.3: errors when the server is not running or the role does not exist; PostgreSQL user names are separate from operating system accounts
1.4 Accessing a Database: psql is the interactive terminal program; psql mydb connects; without a name it defaults to the user account name (o2, simulator behavior for bare psql)
1.4: greeting 'psql (18.6)' and 'Type "help" for help.', prompt mydb=> or mydb=# for a superuser; SELECT version(); output format used by the simulator
1.4: internal commands begin with a backslash and are not SQL; \q quits psql (o3)
psql options -d dbname, -h host, -p port (default usually 5432), -U username (simulator options, cheat sheet)
psql: commands are sent at the command-terminating semicolon; an end of line does not terminate a command (continuation prompt, %R in PROMPT2)
Meta-commands \l (list databases), \dt and \d [pattern] (list and describe relations), \q (quit) (o3)
